check: verify the Golden seed checklist entry's method is executable, after the height6000 entry turned out not to be
why: One entry's howToRunIt described a configuration route that does not exist here. That makes the others worth the same check rather than the same trust.
theEntrySays: Drive the S1C traversal with a fixed non-default seed via -Ps1cSeed and -Ps1cRealWall, the same path the certified seed 17 run took.
bothFlagsExist: -Ps1cSeed is read at smoke-tests.gradle line 27 with a default of 9282026, and -Ps1cRealWall at line 25 with a default of false. Both are real properties.
theMechanismWorksAsDescribed: Line 200 appends level-seed with the actual seed to server.properties when realWall is set. In a properties file the last occurrence wins, so the appended value overrides the template's level-seed=9282026 - which is how a non-default seed takes effect.

aRecordedRunUsedExactlyThis.verdict: The entry names both flags and they appear together in a recorded command, so the method is executable as written.

aDiscrepancyThatResolved: The traversal certificate records seed 17 while the gradle default is 9282026, which looked like a contradiction. It is not: the run passed -Ps1cSeed=17, and seed 17 also appears in the sibling inputs and execution files for that run, so the certificate is reporting the seed actually used rather than the default.
contrastWithTheHeightEntry: That entry described selecting a world height, for which no property exists. This one describes selecting a seed, for which one does and has been used. The difference is only visible by checking each against the code.
